description: Full feature pipeline following the Roki multi-phase pattern: single-pass requirements, a design loop with a dedicated design reviewer, an implementation plan, a code loop with two-model semantic review plus aggregation, and a requirements-based validation gate. The loops and the validation gate are fail-closed: exhausting a review loop without an APPROVED verdict, or a FAIL/missing validation verdict, aborts the run instead of completing it. Does not use Kiro spec sessions — plain workflow steps. Every referenced agent is bundled (wf-design, wf-design-reviewer, wf-planner, wf-coder, semantic_reviewer, wf-review-aggregator), so this recipe is runnable in any workspace. Inputs: 'task' (the feature request) and 'workdir' (absolute path of the repo to work in; if empty the setup step falls back to the current workspace root). A leading setup step creates a fresh timestamped run folder, so artifacts are written under <workdir>/.agents/pipeline/<yyyy-mm-dd_HH-MM-SS>/ — one isolated folder per run, so no stale files from a previous run bias a reviewer or make the first draft look like a revision.
name: feature-pipeline

steps.prompt:
You are the setup step for a feature pipeline run. Do ONLY this, nothing else:
1. Determine the base directory: if {{workdir}} is a non-empty absolute path, use it; otherwise use the current workspace root (an absolute path).
2. Compute a run timestamp string in the format YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS (e.g. `date +%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S`).
3. Create the directory <base>/.agents/pipeline/<timestamp>/ with `mkdir -p`.

Your ENTIRE final response MUST be exactly that absolute directory path and NOTHING else - no prose, no quotes, no backticks, no trailing slash, no trailing punctuation or newline commentary. Later steps consume this exact string as the run directory.

Feature request: {{task}}

Repo: {{workdir}}. Analyze this request and author the REQUIREMENTS document. Write it to {{setup.output}}/01-requirements.md. Scale the output to the task's complexity. If the request is ambiguous, infer reasonable requirements and note your assumptions explicitly — the design review will catch anything that doesn't hold up. Do not design or implement.

Repo: {{workdir}}. Review the design at {{artifacts.design}} against the requirements at {{artifacts.requirements}}. Verify the design's claims about existing code against the actual source in {{workdir}} — do not take its word. Write the full review (numbered findings with HIGH/MEDIUM/NIT severities and concrete fixes, plus Verified Assumptions and Unverified/Wrong Assumptions sections) to {{setup.output}}/03-design-review.md, and the machine verdict to {{setup.output}}/design-review.json as { "verdict": "APPROVED" | "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [...] }. The verdict is mechanical: any HIGH or MEDIUM finding means CHANGES_REQUESTED; zero means APPROVED.

Repo: {{workdir}}. From the approved design at {{artifacts.design}}, write an ordered implementation plan to {{setup.output}}/04-plan.md. Break the work into small, independently verifiable items, each with a "done" checkbox, the files it touches, and how to verify it.

Repo: {{workdir}}. Implement the ENTIRE plan at {{artifacts.plan}}: every unchecked item, checking each off in the plan file as you complete it. Follow the design at {{artifacts.design}} — do not substitute technologies the design locked. If a review exists at {{setup.output}}/code-review.json with verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED, first address every finding in it — the run directory is fresh for this run, so a review file present there always means a genuine loop-back within THIS run, never a stale file from an earlier one. Build and run the relevant tests after each item.

Before finishing, write or update {{setup.output}}/05-code-summary.md: what was implemented, any deviations from the design (with reasons), and a "Tests Run" section listing every verification command with its actual output. Commit the work.

branches.prompt:
Repo: {{workdir}}. Review the changes made for this feature ({{task}}) on the current branch. Obtain the diff yourself: `git -C {{workdir}} diff` for uncommitted work plus the branch's commits against the repo's main/mainline. Perform the full semantic review with every standard section: Summary, High-level view (narrative organized by concern, not by file), and Details. Write your complete review to {{setup.output}}/code-review-fable.md.

ANTI-BIAS: Do NOT read, open, or reference the other reviewer's file. Specifically do NOT read {{setup.output}}/code-review-gpt.md. Only write your own file.

Repo: {{workdir}}. Review the changes made for this feature ({{task}}) on the current branch. Obtain the diff yourself: `git -C {{workdir}} diff` for uncommitted work plus the branch's commits against the repo's main/mainline. Perform the full semantic review with every standard section: Summary, High-level view (narrative organized by concern, not by file), and Details. Write your complete review to {{setup.output}}/code-review-gpt.md.

ANTI-BIAS: Do NOT read, open, or reference the other reviewer's file. Specifically do NOT read {{setup.output}}/code-review-fable.md. Only write your own file.

steps.prompt: Read the two independent reviews at {{artifacts.review_fable}} and {{artifacts.review_gpt}}. Dedupe overlapping findings — both reviewers raising the same issue means higher confidence. Then check the plan at {{artifacts.plan}}. Write {{setup.output}}/code-review.json: verdict "APPROVED" only when there are no blocking findings AND every plan item is checked done; otherwise "CHANGES_REQUESTED" with the merged findings and the unchecked items.

Repo: {{workdir}}. Final validation gate for the feature ({{task}}). Read the requirements at {{artifacts.requirements}} and the code summary at {{artifacts.code_summary}} — NOT the design. For each acceptance criterion: if the code summary's "Tests Run" section directly covers it with a command and its output, you may accept that as evidence (note it); otherwise verify it yourself. Always run at least one end-to-end check yourself as a smoke test, plus the project's full build and test suite. Drift check: does the result match what the user asked for; were requirements dropped or scope added without justification? Write {{setup.output}}/06-validation.md and {{setup.output}}/validation.json as { "verdict": "PASS" | "FAIL", "criteria": [...], "drift": [...] }. Do not fix code in this step — report honestly. Always write validation.json — the workflow gate reads its verdict; a missing file or a FAIL verdict aborts the run.
